comparison: Perfect agreement on cohort characteristics (C1-C4). Both evaluations support these descriptive statistics without challenge. Peer reviewers specifically praised the inclusive nature of the cohort.
Agreement on biphasic decay findings (C10-C14). Both evaluations support the temporal dynamics and modeling approach. Peer reviewers accepted findings after methodological concerns were addressed.

Divergent evaluation of correlation strength. OpenEval marks correlations (C17-C24) as SUPPORTED with acknowledgment of weak-to-moderate magnitude. Peer reviewers mark as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing weakness (Spearman ~0.3) and 'not a very strong signal' despite statistical significance.

Partial agreement on differential associations (C25-C30). Both support the CD127-intact reservoir finding (C28, C30). However, OpenEval evaluates all claims C25-C30 as SUPPORTED while peer review only explicitly addresses C28 and C30, with concerns about other correlations addressed in R3.
Overlapping claims C26 and C29 show divergence. OpenEval includes these in SUPPORTED evaluation, while peer reviewers group them with other weak correlations marked as UNCERTAIN.

Agreement on LOCO analysis findings (C32-C38). Both evaluations support the results despite weak explanatory power. Peer reviewers note categorical classification is 'hard to interpret' but do not challenge the findings.

Divergent evaluation of ROC analysis (C39-C43). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED with clear data presentation. Peer reviewers mark as UNCERTAIN, noting weak predictive signal and challenging interpretation of 70-80% prediction levels for categorical variables.
Agreement on clustering analysis (C44-C52). Both evaluations support the two-cluster identification and characterization, though peer reviewers note overall weak signal across all analyses.

Significant divergence on decision tree utility (C53-C56). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED citing 83.5% accuracy and significant group differences. Peer reviewers mark as UNCERTAIN, questioning clinical utility of categorical classification and above/below median predictions.

Divergence on intact HIV DNA decision tree (C57-C59). OpenEval supports comparable accuracy despite weaker correlations. Peer reviewers group with other decision trees (R8) and question interpretability of categorical approach.

Divergence on percentage intact decision tree (C60-C62). OpenEval supports similar accuracy and significant differences. Peer reviewers group with other decision trees and express concerns about non-standard qualitative characterization.

Agreement on modest predictive performance (C63, C65). Both mark as UNCERTAIN or acknowledge limitations. OpenEval notes ~70% accuracy is modest, peer reviewers emphasize ML algorithms don't outperform classic methods and cannot reveal relationships that don't exist.

Strong agreement on study limitations (C85-C96). OpenEval supports comprehensive acknowledgment of limitations. Peer reviewers explicitly agree, stating authors 'fairly describe the results' and acknowledge weak signal despite detailed methods.

Agreement on uncertain causal inference (C97-C98). Both mark as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes cross-sectional design limits causal claims. Peer reviewers emphasize weak associations and that relationships 'have been shown previously' with limited strength.
OpenEval evaluated background/literature claims (C66-C78) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.
OpenEval evaluated CD127 biology background and need for further investigation (C79-C84) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval identified explicitly speculative claims (C72, C73, C22, C27, C92) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are reasonable hypotheses but unproven mechanisms. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressing these speculative claims.
